issues.failure_explanation: The matrix ι⁺ is 2k×2n, so (ι⁺)ᵀ is 2n×2k and J₂ₙ is 2n×2n. The product (ι⁺)ᵀ J₂ₙ is undefined because the inner dimensions (2k and 2n) do not match. The condition as written has no mathematical meaning.

failure_location.quote: The symplectic pseudo-inverse $\iota^+$ is uniquely defined by the condition $\iota^+ \iota = I_{2k}$ and satisfies $(\iota^+)^T J_{2n} \iota^+ = J_{2k}$, ensuring that the inverse mapping preserves symplectic structure on the embedded submanifold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the second condition with a dimensionally consistent one, e.g. ι⁺ J₂ₙ (ι⁺)ᵀ = J₂ₖ (which holds for the standard inclusion), or simply delete the erroneous clause since ι⁺ι=I₂ₖ already fixes the map.
issues.overall_effect: The stated symplectic compatibility condition on ι⁺ is vacuous/undefined. The primary definition ι⁺ι=I₂ₖ remains valid and the actual use of ι⁺ as a coordinate projection is unambiguous, so no downstream computation is broken, but the stated guarantee is not a well-formed mathematical assertion.
issues.title: Symplectic pseudo-inverse condition is dimensionally inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A single-line correction to a secondary characterisation; the primary definition and all actual uses of ι⁺ are unaffected, so no substantive claim or guarantee is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The universal approximation capability of H\'enonNets implies that any symplectic diffeomorphism, including the nonlinear embedding defined above, can be approximated arbitrarily closely by composing a fixed linear embedding with H\'enonNet transformations.
Let $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{2k}\to \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be an arbitrary symplectic embedding defined on a compact domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{2k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims density of {H∘G∘ι} in the space of symplectic embeddings R^{2k}→R^{2n}. The only justification given conflates symplectic diffeomorphisms of R^{2n} (the target of Turaev's approximation theorem) with symplectic embeddings of R^{2k} into R^{2n} (dimensionally different objects). The nontrivial step—extending an arbitrary symplectic embedding to a symplectomorphism of the ambient space so that Turaev's density applies—requires the symplectic isotopy extension theorem or equivalent, which is neither cited nor proved. No proof of the stated theorem is provided.

failure_location.quote: For any $\varepsilon>0$, there exist parameters of \(\iota, \mathcal{G},\) and \(\text{H}\)  such that the composite map \(\sigma\) defined in \eqref{eq:composite} satisfies

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a proof by citing and applying the symplectic isotopy extension theorem (e.g. Gromov's theorem) to show any symplectic embedding Φ:R^{2k}→R^{2n} factors as F∘ι for some symplectomorphism F of R^{2n}, then invoke Turaev's density result for F. Alternatively, weaken the theorem to state density in the C⁰ topology on compact sets with a reference to the extension step.
issues.overall_effect: The theoretical guarantee that the composite architecture can approximate any symplectic embedding with exact symplecticity is unsupported. The practical method still functions (training can find good embeddings), but the advertised universality is an unestablished claim.
issues.title: Universal approximation theorem stated without valid proof
issues.why_classification: The repair requires citing and correctly applying a nontrivial symplectic-geometry result (isotopy extension) that is absent from the source, but it does not change the theorem's conclusion or require new proof architecture; a contained argument suffices.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: q_{t}(x, t, \omega)=p(x, t, \\omega) \\ p_{t}(x, t, \omega)=\omega^2 q_{x x}(x, t, \\omega)
\frac{d}{d t} \mathbf{z}=\bbJ_{2 N} \nabla_{\bf z} H({\bf z})=\bbJ_{2 N} L \, \mathbf{z}

issues.failure_explanation: With state z=(q₁,…,q_N,p₁,…,p_N) and J₂N=[[0,I],[-I,0]], the system z_t=J₂N·L·z with L=diag(I_N,ω²D_xx) yields q_t=ω²D_xx·p and p_t=−q, not the wave equation q_t=p, p_t=ω²D_xx·q. Moreover, the gradient of the stated Hamiltonian H is (−ω²Δx·D_xx·q, Δx·p)ᵀ, which equals neither Lz nor the wave-equation right-hand side. The correct L should be diag(−ω²D_xx, I_N). The same structural error appears in ex:param-linear with κ(ω) in place of ω².
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace L with diag(−ω²D_xx, I_N) (and diag(−κ(ω)D_xx, I_N) in the parametric example) so that J₂N·L·z=(p, ω²D_xx·q), and correct the Hamiltonian to H=½Σ[p_i²+ω²(q_i−q_{i−1})²/Δx²] so that ∇_z H=Lz. All numerical experiments must then be re-run.
issues.overall_effect: Both wave-equation examples solve the wrong ODE. All reconstruction MSEs, Hamiltonian-conservation plots, and trajectory figures in Examples 1 and 2 correspond to a different Hamiltonian system (q_t=ω²D_xx p, p_t=−q), not the stated wave equation. The claim that the method accurately resolves the wave equation is unsupported by the stated discretisation.
issues.title: Discrete L-matrix does not produce wave-equation dynamics
issues.why_classification: The discrete system central to two of the three numerical experiments is not the PDE the paper claims to discretise; the correction changes the ODE being solved, invalidating all quantitative results in those examples. No local tweak preserves the stated system.

issues.failure_explanation: The canonical-form equations q_t=p_xx+ε(p²+q²)p, p_t=−q_xx−ε(p²+q²)q are generated by the Hamiltonian H=∫[½(q_x²+p_x²)+ε/4(p²+q²)²]dx. The paper's H_cont has coefficients 1 and ε/2 instead of ½ and ε/4, making it exactly twice the correct Hamiltonian. The functional derivatives δH_cont/δp and δH_cont/δq are therefore twice those of the correct H, producing dynamics at twice the speed of the NLS.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert factors of ½ in the gradient term and change ε/2 to ε/4 in the nonlinear term: H_cont=∫[½(q_x²+p_x²)+ε/4(q²+p²)²]dx.
issues.overall_effect: The stated continuous Hamiltonian is inconsistent with the stated canonical-form equations. Any reference to 'the Hamiltonian' of the NLS in the paper points to a quantity that is 2× the true energy, though the qualitative conservation property (dH/dt=0) is unaffected by the constant rescaling.
issues.title: Continuous Hamiltonian for NLS is off by a factor of two
issues.why_classification: A constant rescaling of the Hamiltonian does not change its conservation property or the symplectic structure; the one-line coefficient correction restores consistency with the canonical form without altering any conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The NLS nonlinearity is ε|u|²u, which in real variables gives ε(p²+q²)p and ε(p²+q²)q. The ODE z_t=J(Lz+g(z)) with the stated g(z) produces the nonlinear terms (p²+q²)p and −(p²+q²)q without the factor ε, so the simulated nonlinearity has unit strength regardless of the parameter ε∈[0.9,1.1] the paper claims to vary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Multiply every component of g(z) by ε: g(z)=(ε(q_i²+p_i²)q_i, ε(q_i²+p_i²)p_i). Re-run the numerical experiment.
issues.overall_effect: The Schrödinger experiment does not actually vary the NLS nonlinearity strength; all 500 'parametric' trajectories use ε=1 in the dynamics. The claimed parametric study and the Hamiltonian-conservation results for the NLS example are computed for the wrong nonlinearity.
issues.title: Nonlinear vector g(z) in Schrödinger discretisation omits the parameter ε
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single-factor insertion, but it changes the ODE being solved for every ε≠1, invalidating the parametric results. For ε≈1 the qualitative behaviour is similar, so the repair avoids a major architectural change but still requires re-running experiments.

issues.failure_explanation: Two structural errors: (1) The gradient-energy terms are written as (q_{i−1}q_i−q_i²)²/Δx² = q_i²(q_{i−1}−q_i)²/Δx², which vanish whenever q_i=0 regardless of the gradient and do not discretise ∫q_x² dx; the correct term is (q_i−q_{i−1})²/Δx² (or a symmetric variant). (2) The nonlinear term is ε/4(p_i²+q_i²), which is quadratic in the state, whereas the NLS cubic nonlinearity |u|²u requires the quartic Hamiltonian term ε/4(p_i²+q_i²)². The stated H(z) is not the Hamiltonian generating the ODE z_t=J(Lz+g(z)), and it does not approximate the continuous NLS energy.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the discrete Hamiltonian with H(z)=Δx·Σ[½((q_i−q_{i−1})²+(p_i−p_{i−1})²)/Δx² + ε/4(p_i²+q_i²)²] (or an equivalent second-order discretisation of the continuous NLS energy). Re-evaluate the conservation plots.
issues.overall_effect: The Hamiltonian-conservation loss L_ham and the 'Hamiltonian in time' / 'Hamiltonian deviation' plots in Figure schro_ham evaluate the wrong functional. The paper's claim that the method 'effectively preserves the underlying Hamiltonian structure' in the NLS example is based on a formula that does not represent the NLS energy.
issues.title: Discrete Hamiltonian for Schrödinger has structurally incorrect gradient and nonlinear terms
issues.why_classification: The formula is wrong in two independent structural ways (extra q_i/p_i factors in the gradient term, missing square in the nonlinear term). No single-factor correction fixes it; the entire expression must be rewritten. The Hamiltonian-conservation results central to the paper's structure-preserving claim are thereby invalidated for the NLS example.
